subject: ClearLedger: Incident notification and request for IRP evidence
messages:
From: sam.green@clearledger.com
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com; ops@clearledger.com
Cc: security@clearledger.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:12:05 -0700
Subject: Unusual API traffic spike — possible credential misuse

Hi Aisha / Redwood team,

We saw a ~7x spike in token generation and embedding calls against our integration keys starting ~02:00 UTC. Volume pattern looks automated and a handful of requests returned 401 errors while many succeeded. We're still investigating, but wanted to notify you and request any telemetry / IR artifacts you can share quickly (api keys used, IPs, headers, token-rotation logs).

We are treating this as a suspected credential misuse event and will likely need a short incident report (timeline + actions) to satisfy our internal audit and support our SIG / CAIQ submission. Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Thanks — Sam
Sam Green
CTO, ClearLedger
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
To: sam.green@clearledger.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:36:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic spike — possible credential misuse

Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and sorry you're dealing with this. We confirm receipt and have opened an internal investigation. Immediate actions we're taking: 

- Rotating any live integration tokens tied to your account (we will not rotate transient platform service tokens without explicit consent).
- Pulling request logs, auth events, and edge IPs for the window you mentioned; will share a sanitized extract.
- Escalating to our SOC engineer (cc: Karthik) and Security Ops (cc: Marissa) for a full IRP package.

Can you confirm a safe email for exchange of artifacts (if you prefer secure bucket / SFTP) and whether you need a signed attestation for your auditors? We'll aim to have a preliminary timeline within 4 business hours.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 10:05:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic spike — possible credential misuse

Aisha / team — triage notes below: 

1) Initial telemetry (pulled): auth events show 3 API keys used from two distinct IP blocks (us-west and eu-central) between 01:48–02:23 UTC. Several failed 401 attempts preceded the successful calls by ~6 minutes.
2) We have a preliminary list of request IDs and client_user_agent values — attaching a sanitized log extract as redwood_api_access_spike_20270227.log.
3) No evidence of a host compromise on Redwood side; pattern looks like key exfiltration or reuse.

Next asks: Sam — please confirm whether ClearLedger rotated keys prior to 02/27-02:00 UTC. If not, we recommend immediate rotation and blocking the three keys in question. We'll prepare an IRP evidence package (control mappings to SOC 2 categories, timeline, and mitigations) and share a short signed summary.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SOC/Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

On Sat, Feb 27, 2027 at 09:36 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and sorry you're dealing with this. We confirm receipt and
> have opened an internal investigation. Immediate actions we're taking: ...
From: sam.green@clearledger.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com; aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: security@clearledger.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 12:08:44 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic spike — possible credential misuse

Thanks Karthik — we did not rotate keys in that window. The integration key list matches the IDs you shared. We've rotated all integration keys now and revoked the affected keys.

For artifact transfer, please upload sanitized logs to the secure bucket link below (we control access):
https://s3.clearledger.com/incident-uploads/CL-20270227

Also can you include the mapping to SOC 2 CC7 / CC6 controls in the packet — our compliance team will want the crosswalk for their SIG answers.

- Sam
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: sam.green@clearledger.com; aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 08:17:01 -07:00
Subject: IR evidence packet: timeline, control crosswalk, and mitigation steps

Hi Sam — attaching a short IRP summary (irp-summary-clearledger-20270228.pdf) and the sanitized log extract (redwood_api_access_spike_20270227.log). Highlights: 

- Timeline (UTC): 01:48 auth failures -> 01:54 first successful request -> 02:23 surge ends.
- Root cause: suspected exfiltration of an integration key; no indication of plane-level infra compromise.
- Actions taken: 02:30 revoked affected keys, 03:10 enforced token rotation guidance for customer, 04:15 added IP denylist rules at edge for the two offending CIDR blocks.
- SOC 2 mapping: included is a CC6/CC7 crosswalk pointing to our auth rotation, key management, and telemetry retention controls.

Marissa has signed the short attestation for timeline and actions; if you need a DocuSign copy, request and we'll route it through Legal.

Attachments (sanitized): redwood_api_access_spike_20270227.log (CSV), irp-summary-clearledger-20270228.pdf (pdf), auth-token-rotation-checklist.pdf

Please confirm receipt and if you need additional artifacts (raw edge logs, full trace IDs).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Security Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
From: sam.green@clearledger.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com; aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: security@clearledger.com
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IR evidence packet: timeline, control crosswalk, and mitigation steps

Received and appreciated — the packet meets our audit needs for now. Two follow-ups: 1) Can we get a short paragraph describing retention windows for auth logs (for our SIG answer)? 2) Would Redwood provide a brief post-incident note we can share with our customers (high level, sanitized)?

If you can send those by EOD tomorrow we'll be able to close our internal finding and update our compliance tracker.

Sam
Sam Green
CTO, ClearLedger
